purpose: A list of frames no tilt could reconcile, gathered for plan 5 -- a SYMPTOM, not a per-frame lens measurement. This plan's pre-flight already showed that fitting a lens (fov) alongside pitch is degenerate on real frames (see sensitivityDegPerDegRef), so no single conversion coefficient is offered here and none should be inferred from this file. Nobody acts on this in plan 4e -- meta.photoFovLong is not edited by either task 3 or task 4.
fixRound: REWRITTEN 2026-08-22 in task 4's fix round. The version this replaces was built on kings-court's discarded derivation and carried two problems. (1) It reported willNotConvergeCount 0 for both apartments. That was true of the record as it then stood, but the record was wrong: all four of kings-court's tilt-confirmed spots had been fitted between two DIFFERENT physical objects, and re-deriving them produced this plan's first two genuine will-not-converge spots, which are the strongest lens evidence it has. (2) It gave kings-court 3.webp a bestResidualRows of 0.0932 for a landmark the same file said was never confidently identified -- a bare number that invites a reader to treat it as a measurement. It is removed; every bestResidualRows below is either a real same-object measurement or null.

willNotConvergeCount.note: MEASURED, from each apartment's own -derivation.json outcomeTally.willNotConverge. kings-court: 2.webp and 20.webp. serenity: none -- every serenity spot with an identifiable landmark converged to tilt-confirmed or level-confirmed once swept, and that is reported as it stands rather than forced into this schema. The kings-court pair is a NEW and stronger kind of evidence than a bare non-convergence: on each of those two spots, TWO landmarks were named and crop-confirmed as the same physical object in both frames, measured at the SAME column across the SAME nine captures, and each has a clean interior minimum -- and the two minima are 9 degrees apart on 2.webp and 6-9 degrees apart on 20.webp. A single camera has one tilt. Two same-object landmarks in one frame demanding different tilts cannot be explained by tilt at all, and the residual scales with distance from the principal point, which is the signature of a focal-length difference. Solving 2.webp's two rows simultaneously in angle space needs a focal-length factor of roughly 2.2-2.4 between render and photograph. THAT IS STILL NOT A LENS MEASUREMENT -- it is a two-point estimate from one frame, it assumes the render's own geometry is right, and the pre-flight already showed a two-parameter fit is degenerate. It is offered as a direction and a magnitude class, nothing more.
